content.value_statement: Ad teams can waste spend on tests with weak hypotheses, thin samples, or unclear significance. This skill turns campaign inputs into a test plan, readout, and decision gate.
actual_capabilities: Creates falsifiable hypotheses for paid advertising tests.
Builds A/B/n variant matrices that isolate one changed variable.
Plans sample size, duration, alpha, power, and minimum detectable effect.
Defines primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics for each test.
Documents significance methods for completed user-provided results.
Applies promote, kill, keep-control, or retest decisions.
limitations: It does not create the ad creative or landing page variants.
It depends on accurate user-provided baselines, traffic, and result exports.
It cannot guarantee causal validity when audiences or holdouts are flawed.
It is not a replacement for platform tracking, attribution, or legal review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Landing Page Test
use_cases.description: Turn a conversion goal, baseline rate, and proposed page change into a complete A/B test plan.

use_cases.title: Read Out Finished Results
use_cases.description: Evaluate exported sessions and conversions, then decide whether to promote, kill, or retest a variant.

use_cases.title: Design an Incrementality Holdout
use_cases.description: Structure a treated group and holdout group with metrics, guardrails, duration, and decision rules.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Simple A/B Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner plan for one landing page change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B test for our landing page hero. Baseline CVR is 3 percent, traffic is 1,200 sessions per day, and we want a 15 percent lift.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Creative Variants
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate plan for several ad concepts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a test plan for four paid social creative variants. Goal is prospecting, primary metric is CTR, and daily impressions are about 80,000.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Test Results
prompt_templates.scenario: Use completed counts to make a decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read out these completed test results: control had 18,000 sessions and 540 conversions; variant B had 17,800 sessions and 615 conversions. Minimum practical lift was 10 percent.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Incrementality Measurement
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced design with holdouts and guardrails.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a geo holdout incrementality test for a new retargeting offer. Include hypothesis, holdout logic, sample size assumptions, guardrails, and a promote or kill rubric.

output_examples.input: A marketer asks for a landing page A/B test with a 3 percent baseline CVR and 15 percent lift target.
output: A falsifiable hypothesis for the single landing page change.
A two-arm variant matrix with the control and changed hero treatment.
A sample-size and duration plan using alpha, power, and traffic assumptions.
A decision gate that requires significance and practical lift.

output_examples.input: An analyst provides completed control and variant conversion counts.
output: A named significance method with shown inputs.
The measured conversion rates and relative lift.
A plain-language promote, kill, keep-control, or inconclusive decision.

output_examples.input: An ecommerce team wants to measure whether a promotion drives incremental sales.
output: A treated-group and holdout structure with matching assumptions.
A duration floor and readout plan for the final decision.

best_practices: Provide baseline rates, traffic volume, and the minimum lift worth acting on.
Keep one changed variable per variant so the winner is explainable.
Pre-commit to sample size, duration, and decision gates before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not stop a test early because interim results look favorable.
Do not test many unrelated changes in one variant and call the cause clear.
Do not promote a statistically significant lift that misses the practical threshold.

faq.question: Can this skill create ad variants?
faq.answer: No. It designs the test and decision logic. Use a creative-building skill to produce the variants.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the goal, baseline rate, traffic volume, minimum lift, and any completed results counts.

faq.question: Can it evaluate finished test results?
faq.answer: Yes. It can read user-provided counts and document a significance method and decision.

faq.question: Does it support incrementality tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure treated and holdout groups, metrics, duration, and decision rules.

faq.question: Does it need platform API access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed to work from manually exported user data.

faq.question: Will it always name a winner?
faq.answer: No. It may recommend kill, keep control, segment, or retest when evidence is weak.
